$comment: What the text shows a Kotlin value written into HTML to be, judged by both editors alike: a val or var set to a string literal, a String call on a declared String, toString on any value, a nested template as weak as its values, a value of a type parameter, and values joined with + at a DSL expression site. A case may give `constants`, the workspace's const val names.

cases.name: a nested template that holds a String is a String in text

issues.message: Kotlin writes ${"$q"} into the HTML as it is. If it can hold text from outside, mark it with + in interpolate { }, which escapes it; if it is markup you built, declare it Html or wrap it in Trusted(...).

cases.name: a nested template that holds a String is a String in the structure

issues.message: Kotlin writes ${"title=\"$q\""} into the markup's own structure: a tag name, an attribute name or a list of attributes. Fine for one chosen in code; a value from outside decides the markup itself, and escaping cannot prevent that.

cases.name: a value of a type parameter may be null: the rewrite is offered all the same

issues.message: Kotlin writes $q into the HTML as it is. If it can hold text from outside, mark it with + in interpolate { }, which escapes it; if it is markup you built, declare it Html or wrap it in Trusted(...). interpolate writes nothing for $q where it is null, and Kotlin writes null.

cases.name: a value joined with + into a DSL expression is judged
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.html.*
fun f(id: String) = elements { div { dataOnClick("@get('/x/" + id + "')") } }

issues.message: Kotlin writes the value `id` into data-on, which Datastar runs as an expression or follows as a signal path. Text from outside becomes code there, even inside quotes. Put the value in an attribute of its own, such as data-label, and read it in the expression with el.dataset.label; only a number or a boolean is safe to write in.

cases.name: a template in a DSL literal joined with + is judged
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.html.*
fun f(id: String) = elements { div { dataOnClick("@get('/x/$id')" + ";") } }

issues.message: Kotlin writes $id into data-on, which Datastar runs as an expression or follows as a signal path. Text from outside becomes code there, even inside quotes. Put the value in an attribute of its own, such as data-label, and read it in the expression with el.dataset.label; only a number or a boolean is safe to write in.

cases.name: toString on any value is a String, refused in an expression
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.* fun f(n: Long) = interpolate("""

""", n.toString())

issues.message: interpolate always throws here: n.toString() lands in data-signals, which Datastar runs as an expression or follows as a signal path, and only a number or a boolean is let in there. Put the value in an attribute of its own, such as data-label, and read it in the expression with el.dataset.label.
